questions.def: Inversion after negative adverbials requires auxiliary verb before subject.
questions.question: Under no circumstances ___ leave the building.

questions.def: Inversion with 'had' to form a perfect conditional question.
questions.question: ___ the report been submitted on time?

questions.def: 'Were you to know' expresses hypothetical past knowledge.
questions.question: ___ you ___ (know) that the exam was postponed?

questions.def: 'Had' initiates an inverted conditional sentence.
questions.question: ___ I known, I would have acted differently.

questions.def: 'Should' introduces a formal, conditional clause with subject-verb inversion.
questions.question: ___ he arrive, please inform me immediately.

questions.def: Inversion after 'never' requires auxiliary verb before the subject.
questions.question: Never I have seen such beauty.

questions.def: 'Did she realize' forms a simple past question correctly.
questions.question: ___ she ___ (realize) the consequences of her actions?

questions.def: Inversion after 'only after' requires auxiliary verb ('will') before subject.
questions.question: Only after the investigation ___ the truth be revealed.

questions.def: 'Why' is correct to ask about the reason for something.
questions.question: ___ is it that you find this so difficult?

questions.def: 'Do they understand' is correct present simple question form.
questions.question: ___ they ___ (understand) the implications of the treaty?

questions.def: Inversion after 'not until' requires 'did' before the subject.
questions.question: Not until the end of the presentation ___ the audience understand the point.

questions.def: 'How' is used to inquire about the manner in which something happened.
questions.question: ___ could he have made such a mistake?

questions.def: 'Did he suspect' is the grammatically correct question.
questions.question: ___ he ___ (suspect) that something was amiss?

questions.def: 'Scarcely...than' is the correct correlative conjunction for inverted sentences.
questions.question: Scarcely had they arrived ___ the rain began.

questions.def: 'For what purpose' is correct for formal inquiry about intention.
questions.question: ___ purpose did he undertake this arduous task?

questions.def: Simple present 'Do you believe' is grammatically correct.
questions.question: ___ you ___ (believe) his explanation?

questions.def: After 'seldom', auxiliary verb precedes subject ('have I').
questions.question: Seldom ___ such dedication in a young researcher.

questions.def: 'To what extent' is the conventional phrase to ask about applicability.
questions.question: To ___ extent are these findings applicable?

questions.def: Simple past 'Did they agree' is grammatically correct.
questions.question: ___ they ___ (agree) to the terms of the contract?

questions.def: 'Were we' starts a conditional clause with subject-verb inversion.
questions.question: Were ___ to fail, the consequences would be severe.

questions.def: 'Why' inquires the reason for inconclusive results.
questions.question: ___ were the results of the experiment inconclusive?

questions.def: 'Did they anticipate' forms a simple past question.
questions.question: ___ they ___ (anticipate) such a positive outcome?

questions.def: Inversion after 'little' requires auxiliary verb ('did') before the subject.
questions.question: Little ___ he know what awaited him.

questions.def: 'What' is the appropriate interrogative for asking about the purpose.
questions.question: ___ is the purpose of this inquiry?

questions.def: After 'were' in conditional clauses, use the base form of the verb.
questions.question: Were they to ___ the contract, what would happen?

questions.def: Inversion with 'under no circumstances' requires 'should' for hypothetical situations.
questions.question: Under no circumstances ___ personal data be shared.

questions.def: Inversion after 'seldom' requires the auxiliary verb before the subject.
questions.question: Seldom he visits, nor does he call.

questions.def: 'Little' as a negative adverbial requires subject-auxiliary inversion.
questions.question: Little ___ they, the danger was imminent.

questions.def: 'Had' requires a past participle for the third conditional.
questions.question: Had I ___ the truth, I would have acted differently.

questions.def: 'Only after' requires inversion using auxiliary verb 'did'.
questions.question: Only after extensive research ___ the solution become apparent.
